title: 401 Unauthorized
meaning: A SIP request was rejected because authentication was missing, invalid, or expired.
causes: SIP trunk or connection credentials are incorrect or out of date
Digest authentication challenge/response did not complete correctly
actions: Open the affected call in Calls → Call History and review the SIP Ladder to see which side issued the 401.
Verify the SIP connection's authentication settings under Voice Channels → SIP Connections.
Confirm the credential configured in Live Hub matches what the receiving system expects.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the SIP Ladder shows Live Hub sent correct credentials and the far end still rejected the request, or if you cannot determine which side issued the 401.

title: 403 Forbidden
meaning: A SIP request was understood but rejected as forbidden. This is a protocol result, not a definitive diagnosis — it can be returned by Live Hub, Microsoft Teams, a carrier, a SIP trunk, or a remote SBC depending on configured policy.
causes: The source IP, trunk, or number is not on the receiving system's allow-list
A policy or routing restriction is blocking the request
The receiving system's own access control rejected it
actions: Review the SIP Ladder in Calls → Call History to identify which side returned the 403.
Check the relevant routing rule under Routing → Routing Rules for reject conditions.
If the far end is a carrier or SIP trunk, confirm the source is authorized on their side.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the SIP Ladder confirms Live Hub sent a valid request and the far end still returned 403, or if you cannot determine which side generated the response.

title: 407 Proxy Authentication Required
meaning: The SIP proxy (commonly a carrier trunk) is requesting authentication before it will process the request.
causes: Proxy authentication credentials are incorrect or outdated
The authentication challenge/response cycle did not complete correctly
actions: Review the SIP Ladder for the affected call to see the 407 challenge and whether a response followed.
Verify the trunk's authentication configuration under Voice Channels → SIP Connections.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if credentials appear correct and the challenge is still failing.

title: 404 Not Found
meaning: The destination address could not be resolved to a valid endpoint.
causes: The dialed number isn't provisioned or is mistyped
No routing rule matches this destination
The number was recently ported or reassigned
actions: Open Routing → Routing Rules and confirm a rule exists that matches the called number.
Confirm the destination number is correctly assigned under Voice Channels.
Check for recent number porting or reassignment.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if a matching routing rule and correctly assigned number both exist and the call still returns 404.

title: 408 Request Timeout
meaning: The destination did not respond to the call request within the time SIP allows, so Live Hub treated the attempt as failed.
causes: Network issue between Live Hub and the destination
The SIP trunk or destination system was unreachable
Carrier-side congestion or outage
actions: Check Alarms and Alarm History for related connectivity warnings.
Retry the call and note whether the timeout is consistent or intermittent.
Review the SIP Ladder to confirm no response was received.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the timeout is consistent, affects multiple destinations, or coincides with an active alarm.
evidence: Whether other destinations are also affected

title: 480 Temporarily Unavailable
meaning: The destination is currently unreachable or not accepting calls. This commonly reflects the destination's own state rather than a Live Hub condition.
causes: The destination endpoint is registered but not currently responding
Do-not-disturb or similar state is active on the destination
actions: Confirm with the destination party whether their endpoint was available at the time.
Retry the call after a short interval.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes only if this occurs consistently for a destination that should be reliably reachable.

title: 481 Call/Transaction Does Not Exist
meaning: A request — often related to a transfer or call update — referenced a call session that the receiving side no longer recognized.
causes: The call had already ended on one side when the request was sent
A transfer or re-invite was processed after the original session ended (a timing/race condition)
actions: Review the SIP Ladder and Call Details for the affected call to see the sequence of events around the failure.
Check whether a transfer or hold/resume action was in progress at the time.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the SIP Ladder if the sequence of events doesn't explain the 481.
evidence: Description of any transfer/hold action involved

title: 482 Loop Detected
meaning: The call request was routed back to a point it had already passed through, forming a loop.
causes: A routing rule or forwarding configuration is pointing back to itself or an earlier hop
Two routing rules or trunks each point back to the other, so the call bounces between them until Live Hub detects the loop
A carrier-side forwarding setting redirects the call back toward Live Hub instead of on to a different destination
actions: Review Routing → Routing Rules for any rule whose destination could point back toward its own origin.
If the destination is a customer PBX, check its call-forwarding configuration.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if routing rules and forwarding configuration both look correct and the loop persists.

title: 484 Address Incomplete
meaning: The dialed number is incomplete or doesn't match the expected format for the routing rule handling it.
causes: A digit or prefix is missing in the dialed number
The routing rule's number-matching criteria don't align with the number format actually being sent
actions: Compare the actual dialed number against the calling/called-number criteria in the matched routing rule.
Confirm the expected number format (with/without country code) for this route.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the number format matches the routing rule's criteria and the call still fails with 484.

title: 487 Request Terminated
meaning: The call attempt was cancelled before it completed — most often because the caller hung up before the destination answered.
causes: Caller-initiated cancellation before answer
A no-answer timer on the caller’s own device or softphone expired and cancelled the attempt
An upstream system (dialer, contact center, or auto-attendant) cancelled the call based on its own logic before the destination answered
actions: Check Call Details for alert duration — a short alert duration followed by 487 is typically expected caller-cancel behavior.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes only if 487 is occurring at an unusually high rate relative to total call volume, which may indicate a different underlying issue.

title: 488 Not Acceptable Here
meaning: The far end could not accept the call as offered — commonly a codec or secure-media mismatch.
causes: No common audio codec between the two sides
A secure media (SRTP) mismatch on a call that requires encryption
actions: Review the SIP Ladder to inspect the SDP offer and answer for the affected call.
Confirm the codec and secure-media settings configured for the relevant voice channel.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the SIP Ladder if the SDP offer and answer don't reveal an obvious mismatch.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: 503 Service Unavailable
meaning: The target system — often a carrier or SIP trunk — is currently unable to accept the call.
causes: Carrier-side outage or maintenance
SBC or trunk overload on the receiving side
actions: Check Alarms and Alarm History for related warnings around the time of the call.
Retry after a short interval and note whether the failure is consistent.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if 503 responses are sustained, affect multiple destinations, or correlate with an active alarm.
evidence: Whether other destinations are also affected

title: 603 Decline
meaning: The call was actively rejected by the far end, rather than simply timing out or being unreachable.
causes: Carrier or destination-side reputation/spam filtering
Explicit policy rejection on the receiving side
actions: Check whether this happens consistently for a specific origination number, which may point to number reputation.
Review Routing → Routing Rules to confirm the call isn't being intentionally rejected by a Live Hub rule.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the call isn't rejected by your own routing configuration and the decline is unexpected or affects multiple destinations.

title: No Answer
meaning: The destination rang but nobody (or nothing) answered before the call attempt timed out or the caller gave up.
causes: The destination device was ringing but not picked up
The destination was offline or unreachable
A forwarding loop caused the call to time out before reaching a live endpoint
actions: Confirm with the destination party whether their device was reachable at the time.
If forwarding is configured on the destination, review it for loops or misconfiguration.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes only if this occurs for a destination confirmed to be online and available.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: Busy
meaning: The destination endpoint rejected the call because it was already engaged on another call.
causes: The line is genuinely in use
A call-waiting or simultaneous-call limit on the destination device was reached, even without the person actively using the line
The destination is a hunt group or queue where every member is currently occupied
actions: If this is unexpected, confirm with the destination whether their line was actually busy at the time.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes only if a line reports busy while confirmed to be idle.

title: Insufficient Funds / Trial Restriction
meaning: A trial account with zero or negative credit becomes inactive. While inactive, bots and SIP connections cannot handle calls, and some Live Hub resources cannot be managed until the balance becomes positive again.
causes: The account is on a trial plan and its credit has reached zero or gone negative
A paid account's prepaid balance has been depleted
actions: Check the account's plan and current balance/credit status.
If on trial, review what credit remains and what triggers activation.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the balance appears positive/active but calling and resource management are still blocked.

title: Call Limit / Maximum Call Duration Reached
meaning: The call was ended automatically after reaching a configured maximum-duration limit. This limit can be set at the account level or on an individual voice entity, and the lower applicable value applies.
causes: A maximum call duration is configured on the account or on the specific phone number, SIP connection, Teams connection, or AI Agent voice path handling the call
This is intentional cost-control or compliance behavior rather than a fault — it guarantees no single call runs indefinitely
A shorter limit configured lower in the hierarchy (for example, on a specific number) can override a longer account-level default
actions: Check for a maximum call duration setting on the relevant voice entity and at the account level.
Confirm the call's actual duration matches the configured limit.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the call ended before reaching any configured maximum-duration value.

title: No Matching Route / Call Rejected By Routing Rule
meaning: The call could not be delivered because no routing rule matched it, or a matched rule was configured to reject the call.
causes: No routing rule's origin/call criteria matches this call
A matching rule exists but is intentionally configured to reject calls meeting that criteria
actions: Open Routing → Routing Rules and review origin, calling/called-number criteria, region, and destination for the expected rule.
Confirm whether any rule is configured to reject this type of call intentionally.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if a rule appears correctly configured to accept and route this call, and it's still failing.

title: Region Mismatch
meaning: Live Hub voice entities participating in the same call must be in compatible regions. Traffic can only be routed between Live Hub entities located in the same region.
causes: The phone number, SIP connection, Teams connection, or bot/AI Agent connection involved in the call are configured in different regions
A number, connection, or agent was recently provisioned in a different region than the rest of the call path — often after a configuration change or a resource created in the wrong region by mistake
actions: Check the configured region of the phone number, SIP connection, Teams connection, and bot/AI Agent connection involved in the call.
Confirm the routing rule's destination region is compatible with the origin.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if all relevant entities appear to be in the same region and the call still fails to route.
evidence: Names/regions of the voice entities involved
related: No Matching Route / Call Rejected By Routing Rule

title: Alternate Route / Routing Group Failover
meaning: A routing group can send a call to an alternate destination when the primary destination doesn't respond. This can result in more than one call record for what the customer experienced as a single call attempt.
causes: The primary destination in a routing group failed to answer or was unavailable, triggering failover to the next-priority destination
This is frequently intentional resiliency design working as configured — the routing group falls back to the next destination specifically so calls aren’t lost when the first choice doesn’t answer
actions: Search for related call records — records sharing the same SID can represent the original attempt and the failover.
Confirm the routing group's configured priorities match the observed behavior.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the failover behavior doesn't match the configured routing group priorities.
related: No Matching Route / Call Rejected By Routing Rule

title: Call Connects But Audio Is Bad or Missing (One-Way Audio / No Audio / Choppy Audio)
meaning: The call signals as connected, but one or both sides hear silence, only one direction has audio, or the audio is choppy/distorted. This is a media-path problem, separate from the signaling issues covered by the SIP response codes above.
causes: The audio path (RTP) between the two sides never established, even though call setup succeeded
A firewall, NAT, or network device is blocking media in one direction
The two sides could not agree on a common audio format (codec) or encryption setting
Network congestion, packet loss, or jitter on either leg of the call
For WebRTC/Teams calls, no usable media path could be found between endpoints (ICE negotiation)
actions: Open the call in Calls → Call History and check whether it shows as connected despite the audio problem.
Review the SIP Ladder to confirm signaling completed normally (a normal ladder alongside bad audio points to a media-path, not a signaling, issue).
Check whether the problem affects one specific call, one specific route/carrier, or all calls — this narrows down where the media path is breaking.
Retry the call and note whether the same result happens consistently.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if signaling completed normally, the problem is not isolated to one destination or network path, and it continues on retry.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call

title: 420 Bad Extension
meaning: The far end sent or expected a call-setup detail (a SIP extension/feature) that the other side does not support.
causes: A feature or header used in call setup isn’t supported by the receiving system
A mismatch between what Live Hub, a SIP trunk, or a carrier each expect during call setup
actions: Open the call in Call History and review the SIP Ladder to see which side sent the unsupported extension.
If this is isolated to one trunk or carrier, check whether anything changed recently in that connection’s configuration.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the SIP Ladder doesn’t make clear which side introduced the unsupported extension, or the issue affects more than one call.
related: 481 Call/Transaction Does Not Exist, Protocol Error, Unspecified

title: 403 Remote Is Disconnected
meaning: The remote endpoint disconnected unexpectedly during the call, sometimes following a timeout on that leg. This is a hangup condition distinct from a policy-based 403 Forbidden.
causes: The far end dropped the connection without a clean call teardown
A prior timeout condition (shown as "last Code: 408") led to the disconnect
A network interruption on the remote side ended the session abruptly
actions: Check the SIP Ladder for the sequence of events immediately before the disconnect.
If a "(last Code: 408)" is shown, treat the 408 as the underlying trigger and check that entry too.
Confirm whether this is isolated to one destination/carrier or happening broadly.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if this is happening across multiple destinations or carriers, or the SIP Ladder doesn’t explain the disconnect.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call
related: 408 Request Timeout, Call Connects But Audio Is Bad or Missing

title: Unallocated (Unassigned) Number
meaning: The dialed number doesn’t exist or hasn’t been assigned to anyone on the receiving network — this is a carrier-level result, not a Live Hub routing failure.
causes: The number was mistyped or is genuinely not in service
A number was ported or deactivated recently and the destination network hasn’t updated
actions: Confirm the dialed number is correct, including country/area code.
If this is a known, previously-working number, check whether it was recently ported or deactivated.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the number is confirmed correct and in service, but calls still fail with this result.
related: 404 Not Found, No Matching Route / Call Rejected By Routing Rule

title: Answering Machine Detected
meaning: The call reached a voicemail system or automated answering service rather than a live person.
causes: Answering machine detection identified voicemail/greeting audio patterns on the call
A legitimate live answer with a short or scripted-sounding greeting can occasionally be misclassified as a machine
actions: If this result is unexpected, confirm answering machine detection is configured the way you intend for this routing rule/flow.
Listen back to the call recording, if available, to confirm the detection was accurate.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if answering machine detection is consistently misclassifying live answers as machines (or vice versa).
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call
related: No Answer, User Did Not Respond

title: Protocol Error, Unspecified
meaning: A call-signaling problem occurred that doesn’t map to one of the named, specific protocol results in this guide.
causes: An edge case or unusual signaling sequence occurred that isn’t covered by a standard named result
This is a catch-all the platform uses when the signaling problem doesn’t match a defined, named result — the raw SIP Ladder is usually needed to pin down the specific case
actions: Open the SIP Ladder for the call and look for anything unusual immediately before the failure.
Check whether the issue is reproducible or a one-off.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the SIP Ladder — this result usually needs the raw signaling trace to diagnose further.

title: Call Reached Wrong Destination
meaning: The call was delivered somewhere other than the expected destination.
causes: A different routing rule than expected matched the call (based on origin, calling/called number, or region)
Rule priority/order caused an earlier rule to match first
actions: Open Routing → Routing Rules and check origin, calling/called-number criteria, and destination for every rule that could plausibly match this call.
Confirm which rule actually matched using the call record in Call History.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the routing rules appear correctly configured and the call still reaches the wrong destination.
related: No Matching Route / Call Rejected By Routing Rule

title: Expected Service Not Applied (Recording / Translation / Assist Bot)
status: Expected Service Not Applied (Recording / Translation / Assist Bot)
meaning: A call did not receive an additional service — such as recording, external recording, voice translation, Assist bot, or number customization — that was expected.
causes: The matched routing rule doesn't have the relevant service enabled
A different rule than expected matched the call
actions: Open Routing → Routing Rules, identify the rule that matched this call, and confirm the relevant service is enabled on it.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the correct rule is matched and the service is enabled, but it still didn't apply.

title: Teams Connection Not Active
meaning: The Teams connection is not in an Active state. A new connection can briefly show as Creating before becoming Active — this is expected and not an error on its own.
causes: The connection is still being provisioned (Creating)
Tenant authentication or configuration is incomplete
actions: Check the Teams connection status. If it shows Creating, allow time for provisioning to complete before treating it as a failure.
If it remains in a non-Active state for an extended period, review tenant authentication and configuration.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the connection remains non-Active well beyond the expected provisioning time.

title: Teams Call Fails to Connect
meaning: A call involving a Teams participant fails to connect. Teams calls can be inspected using the same Call History and SIP Ladder tools as other calls — start there rather than assuming the issue is on Microsoft's side.
causes: Teams tenant not connected or not authenticated
Teams connection not in Active state
Missing Microsoft license for the user/resource
Phone number not correctly assigned
Live Hub routing rule missing or misconfigured
Region mismatch between the Teams connection and the other voice entity
actions: Locate the call in Calls → Call History and review the SIP Ladder to see which side returned a failure.

Verify: tenant connected and authenticated → Teams connection Active → user/resource provisioned correctly → phone number assigned → required Microsoft licenses present → Teams voice policies/routes configured → Live Hub routing rule exists → regions match.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if Call History and the SIP Ladder don't clearly explain the failure after working through the checks above.
evidence: Affected Teams user or resource account
related: Teams Connection Not Active, Region Mismatch, User Missing Required Microsoft License

title: User Missing Required Microsoft License
meaning: Teams calling requires eligible Microsoft 365 licensing for the affected user or resource account.
causes: The user or resource account doesn't have the required Microsoft license assigned
A license was recently removed, reassigned, or expired in the Microsoft 365 admin center, even if nothing changed on the Live Hub side
Enterprise Voice is enabled in Teams, but the calling plan or Direct Routing license needed alongside it is missing
actions: Check license assignment for the affected user/resource account in your Microsoft 365 admin center.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the required license is confirmed assigned and the issue continues.

title: Teams Number Not Assigned Correctly
meaning: A phone number intended for a Teams user or resource account isn't correctly assigned.
causes: Number assignment wasn't completed in Teams admin or Live Hub
Assignment doesn't match the connection actually being used
actions: Verify the number's assignment in both Live Hub and the Teams admin center.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the number appears correctly assigned in both places and still isn't working.

title: Agent Does Not Respond
status: Bot Err: no bot input for 20000ms
Bot Err: Error: 11 OUT_OF_RANGE: More than 120
meaning: The caller reached the AI Agent, but the agent did not produce a response.
causes: The call never actually reached the agent (telephony/routing layer)
Speech wasn't recognized (STT layer)
The model/LLM didn't produce a response in time
A tool call was invoked and never returned
The provider or model was unavailable
actions: Confirm the call reached the agent in Calls → Call History.
Check AI Agent logs for the conversation.
Review the separate STT, Bot, and TTS latency figures in Call History to identify which layer was slow or unresponsive — do not assume the delay was the LLM without checking.
If a tool was involved, check whether it was called and whether it returned.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the identified failing layer (telephony, STT, LLM, or tool) if the checks above don't resolve it.
related: Speech Not Recognized, Tool Call Failed or Timed Out, AI Provider/Model Unavailable, Conversation Ended at Maximum Turns

title: Conversation Ended at Maximum Turns
meaning: AI Agents have a configurable Max Turns setting limiting the number of user/agent interactions. Once reached, the conversation can close — this is expected configured behavior, not a platform failure.
causes: The configured Max Turns value was reached during a longer-than-expected conversation
This is a deliberate guardrail against runaway or looping conversations, not a platform failure — it caps how long a single conversation can run
actions: Open the agent's configuration and check the Max Turns setting.
Confirm the number of turns in the conversation log against this value.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the conversation ended well before the configured Max Turns value was reached.

title: Empty or Invalid LLM Response
meaning: The configured language model returned an empty or invalid response for a turn in the conversation.
causes: Transient issue with the model provider
Prompt or configuration produced an unexpected response format
actions: Check AI Agent logs for the specific conversation turn to confirm this occurred.
Note whether it's a one-off or repeatable with similar input.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the conversation log if this is repeatable or affecting multiple conversations.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: AI Provider/Model Unavailable
meaning: The underlying AI model or provider configured for the agent was unavailable when needed.
causes: Provider-side outage or degradation
Configured model is deprecated, restricted, or misconfigured
actions: Check AI Agent logs for the conversation to confirm the model/provider involved.
Confirm the configured model is currently valid and available for the account.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the configured model/provider appears correct and valid, and the unavailability persists.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation
related: Empty or Invalid LLM Response, AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached

title: AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached
status: AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached
meaning: A rate or quota limit on the AI provider/model has been reached.
causes: Request volume to the model/provider exceeded the configured or provider-side limit
A burst of concurrent conversations pushed request volume above the provider’s per-minute or per-day allowance
The configured AI provider account may be on a lower usage tier than current call volume requires
actions: Check AI Agent logs around the affected time for rate/quota-related messages.
Review recent conversation volume for the affected agent.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes to review the applicable limit and discuss increasing it if usage is expected to continue at this level.
evidence: Approximate conversation volume at the time
Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: Agent/Conversation Session Expired
meaning: The AI Agent conversation session ended due to inactivity or reaching its maximum allowed duration. This is distinct from a user's sign-in session expiring in the Live Hub portal.
causes: The conversation was inactive for longer than the session timeout allows
The conversation reached its maximum configured duration
actions: Check the conversation log to confirm how long the session was inactive before ending.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the session ended despite active, ongoing conversation.
related: User Authentication Session Expired, WhatsApp Conversation Window Closed

title: Bot/Agent Failed To Start
status: Bot Err: Error starting bot: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND
Bot Err: Error starting bot: Request failed with...
meaning: The AI agent/bot failed to initialize for this conversation before it could begin responding.
causes: The bot platform or endpoint the agent connects to was unreachable (e.g. a DNS/network lookup failure)
A request made during startup failed or was rejected
actions: Confirm nothing changed recently in the agent/bot’s configuration or its connection details.
Check whether this is affecting one specific agent/flow or all of them.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the agent’s configuration hasn’t changed and it consistently fails to start.
related: AI Provider/Model Unavailable, Agent Does Not Respond

title: Bot Platform Communication Failed (Error Posting Activity)
status: Bot Err: Error posting activity: timeout of 100
Bot Err: Error posting activity: timeout of 150
Bot Err: sendStream cannot complete since 'user...
meaning: Live Hub could not successfully send an update (such as the caller’s input) to the bot platform mid-conversation.
causes: The bot platform didn’t respond within the expected time window while Live Hub was sending it an update
A streaming connection to the bot platform was interrupted mid-conversation
actions: Check whether this is happening across many conversations or isolated to one agent/flow.
Confirm nothing changed recently in the bot platform connection or endpoint.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if this is recurring across multiple conversations rather than a one-off.
related: Bot/Agent Failed To Start, Agent Does Not Respond

title: Speech Not Recognized
meaning: The AI Agent did not correctly recognize what the caller said.
causes: Speech-to-text configuration (language, provider) doesn't match what the caller is speaking
Audio quality or background noise affected recognition
STT latency or a service issue on the speech provider side
actions: Open the agent's Speech and Telephony configuration and confirm the configured language matches the caller's language.
Review the STT latency figure for the affected call in Call History.
Listen to the call recording, if available, to assess audio quality.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if language and audio quality both look correct and recognition still fails consistently.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation
related: Agent Does Not Respond, Incorrect Speech Recognition

title: Incorrect Speech Recognition
meaning: The agent recognized speech, but transcribed it incorrectly, leading to an unexpected response.
causes: Accent, background noise, or audio quality affecting STT accuracy
Domain-specific vocabulary not well recognized by the configured STT service
actions: Review the conversation log/transcript to see exactly what was recognized versus what was said.
Check the configured STT language and provider under Speech and Telephony.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with specific examples if misrecognition is frequent and affecting normal, clear speech.
evidence: Example of what was said vs. what was recognized
Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: Agent Cannot Be Interrupted (Barge-In)
meaning: The caller is unable to interrupt the agent while it's speaking.
causes: Barge-in is disabled in the agent's Speech and Telephony configuration
Barge-in can also be unsupported by the specific speech/telephony configuration in use for that agent, separate from whether the setting is toggled on
actions: Open the agent's Speech and Telephony settings and confirm whether barge-in is enabled.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if barge-in is enabled in configuration but interruption still doesn't work.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: DTMF Not Detected
meaning: Touch-tone (DTMF) input from the caller was not detected or acted on by the agent.
causes: DTMF handling isn't configured or enabled for this agent/Flow
The Flow or prompt doesn't define expected behavior for DTMF input
A telephony-layer issue prevented DTMF tones from reaching the agent
actions: Check the agent's Speech and Telephony and Flow configuration for DTMF handling.
Confirm DTMF was actually sent — review the call recording or logs if available.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if DTMF handling is configured correctly and tones are confirmed sent, but still not detected.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation

title: No User Input Event
meaning: AI Agents generate a synthetic event (such as NO-USER-INPUT-1, with incrementing numbers for repeated occurrences) when the caller is silent during a voice conversation. This is expected platform behavior, not an error — how it's handled depends on the agent's prompt or Flow configuration.
causes: The caller was silent and this event fired as designed
The prompt or Flow doesn't handle this event the way you expect (e.g. it should repeat a prompt, transfer, or end the call)
actions: Review the agent's prompt or Flow to see how NO-USER-INPUT events are configured to be handled.
Check the conversation log to see how many NO-USER-INPUT events occurred and what happened after.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the configured handling doesn't match observed behavior.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation
related: DTMF Not Detected, Agent Does Not Respond

title: Call Ends After Fixed Duration (AI Agent)
status: Call Ends After Fixed Duration (AI Agent)
meaning: The call with the AI Agent ends consistently after a set amount of time. This commonly reflects a configured maximum call duration on the agent's Speech and Telephony settings, the voice entity, or the account.
causes: Maximum call duration is configured on the agent, the relevant voice channel, or the account, and the lower applicable value is being enforced
If no limit was intentionally set for this agent, check whether a default account-level maximum is being inherited instead
actions: Check the agent's Speech and Telephony configuration for a maximum call duration setting.
Also check the relevant voice entity and account-level limits.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if no configured maximum duration explains the observed cutoff point.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation
related: Call Limit / Maximum Call Duration Reached

title: Speech-to-Text Service Connection Failed (STT Err)
status: STT Err: Websocket error: WebSocket was closed
STT Err: Unable to contact server. StatusCode:
meaning: The connection to the Speech-to-Text service was lost or couldn’t be established, so the caller’s speech couldn’t be transcribed for this part of the call.
causes: The STT provider’s connection was interrupted or closed unexpectedly
The STT service was unreachable or returned an error status when Live Hub tried to connect
actions: Check whether this is isolated to one call or affecting speech recognition broadly.
If it’s widespread and recent, check whether it lines up with a known STT provider incident.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if this is affecting multiple calls or agents rather than a single occurrence.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call
related: Speech Not Recognized, Text-to-Speech Request Failed (TTS Err)

title: Text-to-Speech Request Failed (TTS Err)
status: TTS Err: 400 Bad Request. Req body: <speak ...
meaning: A request to convert the agent’s response text into spoken audio was rejected as malformed or invalid, so the caller may have heard nothing or a fallback message instead.
causes: The text sent to the Text-to-Speech service contained something it couldn’t process (for example, invalid formatting in the spoken-text markup)
Special characters, unsupported spoken-text markup, or an unexpectedly long response can each trigger this on the Text-to-Speech provider’s side
actions: If this is tied to a specific agent response or prompt, check that response for unusual characters or formatting.
Check whether this is a one-off or consistently tied to the same prompt/response.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if this is consistently tied to a specific prompt or happening across many calls.
evidence: Agent/flow name and the response involved, if known

title: Tool Call Failed or Timed Out
status: Tool Call Failed or Timed Out
meaning: The agent attempted to use a tool to perform an external action, and the tool call failed or didn't return in time.
causes: The tool's target endpoint was unavailable
The request timed out
Authentication to the target endpoint failed
The endpoint returned an error
actions: Review AI Agent logs for the conversation to see the tool call, its parameters, and the returned status/error.
Confirm the target endpoint is reachable and functioning independently of Live Hub.
Check the tool's configured authentication is current.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the sanitized request/response details if the target endpoint is confirmed healthy and the tool call still fails from Live Hub.
related: Agent Does Not Respond, Audio Playback Failed

title: Wrong Tool Selected or Invalid Parameters
status: Wrong Tool Selected or Invalid Parameters
meaning: The agent invoked a tool, but selected the wrong one or generated parameters that didn't match what was expected.
causes: The prompt/instructions don't clearly guide the model on when and how to use the tool
The tool's parameter definitions are ambiguous or incomplete
actions: Review AI Agent logs to see which tool was called and with what parameters.
Review the agent's prompt/instructions and the tool's parameter definitions for clarity.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the tool and parameter configuration look correct and the model still consistently selects the wrong tool.
related: Tool Call Failed or Timed Out

title: Audio Playback Failed (PLAY-URL-FAILED)
meaning: The agent's audio playback tool failed to play a prerecorded audio file. Live Hub documents an exact failure indicator, PLAY-URL-FAILED, which includes the specific reason for the failure.
causes: The audio URL was unreachable
The file format isn't supported
The tool configuration is incorrect
actions: Check AI Agent logs for the PLAY-URL-FAILED message and the specific reason included with it.
Confirm the audio URL is reachable and the file format is supported.
Review the tool's configuration for the affected agent.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the exact PLAY-URL-FAILED reason if the URL and format both check out.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation
related: Tool Call Failed or Timed Out

title: Call Transfer Failed
meaning: The agent attempted to transfer the call and the transfer did not complete successfully.
causes: The transfer target isn't correctly configured
The transfer target didn't answer
A call-control action returned an error
actions: Review AI Agent logs and the SIP Ladder for the transfer attempt.
Confirm the intended transfer target is correctly configured and reachable.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the logs and SIP Ladder if the transfer target is correctly configured and reachable but the transfer still fails.
related: Tool Call Failed or Timed Out

title: Agent Gives Incorrect Answer From Document
status: Agent Gives Incorrect Answer From Document
meaning: The agent answered a question using an attached document, but the answer was wrong or didn't reflect the document's actual content. This is usually a retrieval or content issue, not a platform failure — Live Hub converts source content to Markdown and splits it into chunks, so retrieval quality depends on that processing and configuration.
causes: The document isn't attached to the agent that needs it
The relevant information wasn't captured well during chunking
The wrong retrieval mode is selected for this use case
The question falls outside what the document actually covers
actions: Confirm the document is attached to the correct agent under AI Agents → Documents.
Open AI Agents → Documents → [Document] → Info to inspect the document's status and generated chunks.
Test the same question directly and compare the agent's answer to the source content.
Review the configured retrieval mode for the document.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the document name, the question asked, and the expected vs. actual answer if the document, chunks, and retrieval mode all appear correct.
related: Document Not Accessible or Cannot Be Retrieved

title: Document Not Accessible or Cannot Be Retrieved
status: Document Not Accessible or Cannot Be Retrieved
meaning: A document the agent relies on could not be downloaded, parsed, or made available to the agent.
causes: The source URL is inaccessible
The document failed to parse correctly
The document isn't fully processed yet
actions: Open AI Agents → Documents → [Document] → Info and check its current status.
If the source is a URL, confirm it's currently reachable.
Review generated chunks, where available, to see whether processing completed.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the document status shows a processing failure that persists after re-checking the source.
related: Agent Gives Incorrect Answer From Document

title: Flow Takes Unexpected Path
meaning: A Flow — a deterministic sequence of nodes and transitions — moved to a different node than expected. This is generally a configuration matter (a condition, transition, or extracted variable behaving differently than intended) rather than a platform execution failure.
causes: A transition condition evaluated differently than expected
Variable extraction produced an unexpected value
A fallback path was triggered
A no-user-input event drove the conversation down an unintended path
actions: Review the Flow's node and transition configuration for the path in question.
Check the conversation log to see which conditions and variable values were evaluated at each transition.
If testing, use the Flow's test/preview capability to trace the path step by step.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the conversation log and expected vs. actual path if the Flow logic appears correctly configured and the path is still wrong.
related: No User Input Event, Maximum Transitions Reached

title: Maximum Transitions Reached
meaning: The Flow reached its configured limit on transitions or turns and ended or moved to a fallback path as designed.
causes: The conversation genuinely required more turns than the configured maximum allows
A Flow design issue — such as a transition condition that’s never satisfied — can also cause turns to accumulate without the Flow ever reaching its intended end node
actions: Check the Flow's configured maximum-transition/turn setting against the observed conversation length.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the Flow ended well before the configured maximum was reached.
related: Conversation Ended at Maximum Turns, Flow Takes Unexpected Path

title: Sub-Agent Not Reached / Wrong Agent Responds
status: Sub-Agent Not Reached / Wrong Agent Responds
meaning: In a multi-agent setup, control did not transfer to the expected sub-agent, or a different agent than expected responded.
causes: The sub-agent isn't correctly configured or assigned
Orchestration/prompt logic didn't hand off control as intended
A model/provider-specific limitation affected multi-agent handoff
actions: Identify the main agent and the expected sub-agent for this scenario.
Inspect conversation logs around the point where handoff should have occurred.
Confirm the sub-agent is correctly configured and assigned.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the conversation log if configuration looks correct and handoff still isn't happening as expected.

title: WhatsApp Number Not Connected
meaning: The WhatsApp Business number isn't showing as connected in Live Hub.
causes: The Meta/WhatsApp authorization flow wasn't completed
The connection was disconnected or revoked on the Meta side
actions: Check the number's connection status under Voice Channels → WhatsApp Numbers.
If not connected, complete the WhatsApp/Meta authorization flow again.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the authorization flow completes successfully but the number still doesn't show as connected.

title: WhatsApp Message Failed
meaning: A WhatsApp message could not be delivered to the recipient, and WhatsApp returned a delivery failure rather than a delivered/read receipt.
causes: The customer service window with this recipient has closed and the message isn't an approved template
A template message was used but hasn't been approved
A Meta-side policy or account restriction is in effect
General delivery failure on Meta's side
actions: Check whether the 24-hour conversation window with this recipient is open or closed.
If sending a template, confirm it's approved.
Check the WhatsApp Business Account status for any restriction.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the conversation window is open, the template (if used) is approved, and there's no account restriction, yet the message still fails.
related: WhatsApp Conversation Window Closed, WhatsApp Template Not Approved

title: WhatsApp Conversation Window Closed
meaning: WhatsApp's customer service window closes after a period without a customer reply. Once closed, only approved template messages can be sent until the customer messages again.
causes: More time has passed since the customer's last message than the WhatsApp-defined window allows
The window only resets from a genuine customer-initiated message — an agent or automated reply does not reopen it
actions: Check the timestamp of the customer's last inbound message to confirm whether the window should be open or closed.
If you need to reach the customer, use an approved template message.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the window appears closed despite a recent customer reply.

title: WhatsApp Template Not Approved
meaning: A message template hasn't completed Meta's approval process yet, so it can't be used to start a conversation outside the customer service window.
causes: The template is still pending review
The template was rejected during review
actions: Check the template's status in your WhatsApp template management.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the template shows approved but still can't be used to send messages.

title: WhatsApp Business Account Restricted
meaning: Meta has placed a restriction on the WhatsApp Business Account, which can affect the ability to send messages.
causes: A Meta-side policy or quality restriction has been applied to the business account
Restrictions are commonly triggered by a drop in message quality rating, a spike in blocks/reports from recipients, or a policy violation flagged by Meta’s automated review
actions: Check the WhatsApp Business Account status and any notifications from Meta about the restriction.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes for help understanding the restriction — resolving it typically requires coordination with Meta.

title: Expected Recording Is Missing
meaning: A recording that was expected for a call cannot be found. This isn't automatically a processing failure — recording depends on routing configuration, retention settings, and access permissions, and any of these can explain a missing recording.
causes: The routing rule that matched the call didn't have recording enabled
The call wasn't actually established
The recording has been removed under the account's retention policy
External recording was used instead of Live Hub recording
The viewing user doesn't have permission to access it
actions: Confirm which routing rule matched the call, and whether recording (Live Hub or external) was enabled on it.
Confirm the call was actually established (not just attempted).
Check whether the recording may have been removed under retention/lifecycle settings.
Confirm the current user has permission to view recordings for this call.
Check the recording area within Calls → Call History for this call.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the Call ID if the matched routing rule had recording enabled, retention hasn't expired, and permissions are correct, yet the recording still doesn't appear.
evidence: Current status shown in Call History
related: Recording Retention Expired, Recording Still Processing

title: Recording Still Processing
meaning: The call recording exists but hasn't finished processing yet, so it isn't viewable immediately.
causes: Normal processing delay after call completion
Longer calls, or higher account-wide recording volume at the same time, can extend how long processing takes
actions: Wait a short period and check Call History again for the recording.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the recording remains in a processing state for an extended period.
evidence: How long the recording has shown as processing

title: Recording Retention Expired
meaning: Live Hub can automatically remove outdated recordings and transcripts according to the account's retention configuration. An old recording no longer being available may reflect this lifecycle behavior rather than a fault.
causes: The recording's age exceeded the configured retention period
Retention is usually set account-wide, so if the removal timing is unexpected, the configured period may not match what was assumed when the account was set up
actions: Check the account's configured retention period against the age of the recording you're looking for.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the recording should still be within the retention window but isn't available.

title: Transcript Not Available
meaning: A transcript expected for a call or recording cannot be found.
causes: Transcription wasn't enabled for this call
The transcript is still being generated
The underlying recording is missing or was removed under retention
actions: Confirm transcription was enabled for this call via the matched routing rule or agent configuration.
Check whether the transcript may still be generating.
Confirm the underlying recording exists and hasn't been removed under retention.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the Call ID if transcription was enabled, sufficient time has passed, and the recording exists, but the transcript is still missing.
evidence: Whether transcription was enabled for this call
related: Expected Recording Is Missing, Recording Retention Expired

title: Cannot Sign In (Authentication Failure)
meaning: A user cannot sign in to Live Hub. This is a question of authentication — confirming who the user is — which is distinct from authorization (what they're allowed to do) once signed in.
causes: Incorrect username/password for local authentication
Microsoft/Entra ID authentication issue for organizations using Microsoft sign-in
MFA step not completed successfully
The account is disabled
actions: Confirm which sign-in method applies (local Live Hub credentials vs. Microsoft/Entra ID).
For local sign-in, confirm the username and attempt a password reset if needed.
For Microsoft sign-in, confirm the user can authenticate normally with Microsoft outside of Live Hub.
Confirm MFA, if enabled, is completing successfully.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if credentials and MFA are confirmed correct and sign-in still fails, or if the account may be disabled.

title: Insufficient Permissions For Action
meaning: A signed-in user cannot perform an action or see a menu/resource they expect to. Access to Live Hub resources is controlled through IAM, user groups, and policies — a missing menu or blocked action is typically a permissions matter, not a platform failure.
causes: The user's assigned user group/policy doesn't grant access to this resource or action
The user isn't a member of the account where the resource exists
actions: Check the user's assigned user group(s) and policies under account IAM settings.
Confirm the user is a member of the correct account (especially in parent/subaccount setups).
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the user's assigned permissions should cover this action and it's still blocked.

title: User Authentication Session Expired
meaning: The user's Live Hub portal sign-in session has expired and they need to sign in again. This is separate from an AI Agent conversation session expiring.
causes: Normal session timeout after a period of inactivity or elapsed time
Signing in from a new device or browser, or an administrator-forced sign-out policy, can also end a session earlier than the normal inactivity timeout
actions: Sign in again to start a new session.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if sessions are expiring much faster than expected during active use.

title: API Client Access Denied
meaning: An API Client (a non-human, programmatic user) was denied access to an endpoint or action.
causes: The API Client's assigned user group/permissions don't cover this endpoint or action
The client secret in use is outdated or was rotated
actions: Check the API Client's assigned user group/permissions.
Confirm the client secret configured in the calling system is current — do not send the secret itself anywhere, including to AudioCodes Support.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the API Client name/ID, the endpoint or action attempted, and the HTTP status/error returned if permissions appear correct.

title: Post-Call Analysis Webhook Failed
meaning: A post-call analysis result (such as a summary or structured extraction) failed to deliver to your configured webhook endpoint. Live Hub records a response_status and response_text for each delivery attempt — an HTTP 2xx status means successful transmission, an HTTP 4xx/5xx means the receiving endpoint returned an error, and a status of 700 specifically indicates the delivery attempt timed out.
causes: The receiving endpoint returned an error (4xx/5xx)
The receiving endpoint didn't respond in time (status 700)
The endpoint URL or authentication configured is incorrect
actions: Check the recorded response_status and response_text for the delivery attempt.
If 4xx/5xx, review your endpoint's own logs for why it rejected the request.
If status 700, confirm your endpoint responds quickly enough and is reachable.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if response_status/response_text don't clearly explain the failure, or if you need help confirming what Live Hub actually sent.

title: Third-Party Tool/API Failed
meaning: A call from Live Hub to a connected third-party service (a CRM, ticketing system, or other external API) did not complete successfully.
causes: The third-party service is unavailable
Authentication to the third-party service failed
The request sent didn't match what the service expects
actions: Test the third-party endpoint independently of Live Hub, if possible, to confirm it's healthy.
Confirm authentication/credentials configured for the integration are current.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the sanitized request/response if the third-party endpoint is confirmed healthy and the failure persists from Live Hub.
related: Post-Call Analysis Webhook Failed, Tool Call Failed or Timed Out

title: Account Inactive — Broad Service Failure
meaning: Many unrelated functions are failing at once. Before assuming a technical outage, check account balance and state — a trial account with zero or negative credit becomes inactive, and an inactive account cannot handle calls through bots or SIP connections and blocks management of certain resources.
causes: The account's prepaid balance is depleted
A trial account has reached zero or negative credit
actions: Check the account's plan, balance, and active/inactive status.
Check Alarms and Alarm History for related warnings (e.g. low-funds thresholds).

Once balance/state is ruled out, determine whether the failure affects all calls, one provider, one region, Teams only, one AI provider, one agent, or one routing rule — narrowing the scope before assuming a platform-wide issue.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the account is active with sufficient balance and the broad failure continues.
evidence: Scope of affected functionality (all calls / specific provider / specific region / etc.)

title: Feature Not Available on Current Plan
status: Feature Not Available on Current Plan
meaning: A feature being used isn't included in the account's current plan or entitlement.
causes: The plan doesn't include this feature
The feature requires a specific add-on or tier
actions: Review the account's current plan and entitlements.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes to discuss adding this feature to your plan.

title: Concurrent Call Limit Reached
meaning: New calls are being rejected because the account or a specific voice entity has reached its configured maximum concurrent-call limit.
causes: Call volume has genuinely exceeded the configured concurrency limit
A stuck call that never properly released can occupy a concurrency slot without an active conversation actually happening
actions: Check Alarms and Alarm History for a maximum-concurrent-calls threshold alert.
Review which account/entity the limit applies to.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes to review the current limit and discuss an increase if this volume is expected to continue.
evidence: Approximate call volume at the time

title: CPS Limit Reached
meaning: Calls are failing specifically during bursts because the configured Calls Per Second (CPS) threshold has been exceeded.
causes: A traffic burst exceeded the configured CPS limit for the account or entity
A dialer, bulk campaign, or retry storm — many calls retried in a short window right after a failure — is a common trigger even when total daily volume is normal
actions: Check Alarms and Alarm History for a CPS-related threshold alert.
Review the timing of the failures against known traffic spikes.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes to review the current CPS limit and discuss an increase if bursts like this are expected.

title: Rejected Calls Due to Limit Exceeded
status: Rejected Calls Due to Limit Exceeded
meaning: Calls are being explicitly rejected because a configured limit was exceeded. Live Hub supports alarm thresholds specifically for calls rejected due to limits being exceeded.
causes: Concurrent call, CPS, or another configured limit was exceeded
This is a summary/alarm-level indicator rather than one specific mechanism — check Concurrent Call Limit Reached and CPS Limit Reached individually for which one actually applies
actions: Check Alarms and Alarm History for a rejected-calls-due-to-limit-exceeded alert around the affected time.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes to review which specific limit is being hit and discuss adjusting it.
related: Concurrent Call Limit Reached, CPS Limit Reached

title: AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached (Capacity)
status: AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached (Capacity)
meaning: See AI Agents & Conversations → AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached. Listed here for discoverability under capacity/limit topics.
causes: Request volume to the configured AI model/provider exceeded the applicable limit
The account may be using a shared AI provider quota across multiple agents, so unrelated agents can contribute to hitting the same limit
actions: Review AI Agent logs around the affected time for rate/quota-related messages.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes to review the applicable limit and discuss increasing it.
evidence: Call recording, if one was captured for this call/conversation
related: AI Rate or Quota Limit Reached

title: Phone Number Provisioning Failed
meaning: A new phone number failed to be provisioned onto the account.
causes: The number is already in use elsewhere
A required configuration step wasn't completed
actions: Confirm the number isn't already assigned elsewhere in the account.
Retry the provisioning steps and confirm each required field is completed.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if provisioning continues to fail after confirming the number is available and all required fields are complete.

title: Resource Already Exists
meaning: A resource (such as a routing rule, agent, or connection) could not be created because one with the same name/identifier already exists.
causes: A resource with this name already exists in the account
This commonly happens when a resource was actually created successfully on a previous attempt that appeared to fail, and the retry reused the same name
actions: Search for an existing resource with the same name before creating a new one, and rename if needed.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if no visibly conflicting resource exists and creation still fails with this message.

title: SIP Connection Not Reachable
meaning: A configured SIP connection cannot be reached, affecting calls that depend on it.
causes: The remote SBC or SIP trunk endpoint is down or unreachable
A firewall or network path issue is blocking connectivity
The connection's configuration (address, port, credentials) is incorrect
actions: Check the SIP connection's configuration under Voice Channels → SIP Connections.
Check Alarms and Alarm History for related connectivity alerts.
Confirm with your network/carrier that the remote endpoint is reachable.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the configuration is confirmed correct and the remote endpoint is confirmed reachable, yet Live Hub still can't connect.

title: TLS/Certificate Issue
meaning: A secure connection (TLS) failed to establish, commonly due to a certificate problem.
causes: An expired or soon-to-expire certificate on either side
A certificate not trusted by the receiving party
A hostname/FQDN mismatch
actions: Check the relevant certificate's expiry date and issuing authority.
Confirm the hostname/FQDN in the certificate matches the configuration in use.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the certificate is valid, trusted, and matches, and the TLS failure persists.

title: Unknown Error (Unspecified Platform Failure)
meaning: An unexpected platform-level error occurred and Live Hub could not identify a more specific cause.
causes: An edge case occurred that isn’t mapped to a specific, named error
This is a deliberate catch-all rather than a specific diagnosis — it exists so a call or action doesn’t fail completely silently, even when the platform can’t further classify what happened
actions: Note the exact time and any pattern (same call type, same route, same integration) around when it occurs.
Check Alarms and Alarm History for anything related at the same time.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes — this result doesn’t point to a specific self-service fix, so Support will need to investigate the underlying cause.
evidence: What you observed vs. what you expected

title: Temporary Failure (Transient System Error)
meaning: A short-lived network, carrier, or service issue affected the call or action. Live Hub is explicitly flagging this as transient rather than a persistent failure.
causes: A brief network hiccup, carrier-side blip, or momentary service unavailability occurred
Live Hub distinguishes this from a hard failure specifically because a retry is expected to succeed — if it doesn’t clear on retry, the underlying issue is no longer transient
actions: Retry the call or action — transient failures typically resolve on their own.
If it keeps recurring for the same destination or integration, that’s no longer "temporary" and is worth a closer look.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if this result keeps recurring rather than clearing on retry.

title: Idle Endpoint / Session Inactivity Timeout
meaning: The endpoint on the call or session stopped responding or generating activity, and Live Hub ended it as idle.
causes: The far end stopped sending expected signaling or media activity
A device, app, or integration on one side hung or lost its connection without a clean disconnect
actions: Check whether this is isolated to one endpoint, device, or integration.
If it’s a recurring device or app, confirm it isn’t losing network connectivity mid-session.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if idle-endpoint results are happening across multiple sessions or endpoints without a clear device-side cause.

title: System Recovery After Timeout
meaning: A timeout occurred on the call or session, and Live Hub’s recovery process activated to bring it to a clean end state.
causes: A component or step in the call flow didn’t complete within its expected time window, triggering recovery handling
Seeing this result is itself evidence the recovery mechanism worked as intended — the concerning signal is how often it fires, not that it fired once
actions: Check what the call/session was doing right before this point (which flow step, tool call, or media wait) to see what actually timed out.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if this is affecting a specific flow or integration repeatedly.
evidence: Flow or step where it occurred, if known

title: Internal Call-Leg Timeout (Low-Level)
status: Subsystem Id: ICALLLEG Cause Code: Timeout
meaning: An internal Live Hub call-processing component timed out while handling this call leg. This is a low-level, engineering-style result rather than a customer-configurable one.
causes: An internal processing step for this call leg didn’t complete in time
Because this sits below customer-configurable settings, a recurring pattern is more informative than a single occurrence
actions: Note the exact time and any pattern in what type of call this affects.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the Call ID — this result generally requires backend investigation rather than self-service checks.

title: Interworking Issue, Unspecified
meaning: A compatibility issue occurred between Live Hub and an interconnected carrier or system, without a more specific cause identified.
causes: Two interconnected systems (for example, Live Hub and a carrier network) disagreed on how to handle some part of the call
This can also surface after a carrier or upstream provider makes an unannounced change to their own signaling behavior
actions: Check whether this is isolated to one carrier route or destination.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the Call ID and destination — interworking issues usually need coordination with the carrier or upstream system.

title: Active Alarm on Account
meaning: Live Hub is showing an active alarm on the account. Alarms are early-warning indicators with their own severity levels — Critical, Major, Minor, Warning, or Cleared — used for account-wide monitoring.
causes: A monitored threshold (failed calls, poor-quality calls, concurrency, CPS, rejected calls, remaining funds, etc.) has been crossed
The alarm may reflect a leading indicator — for example, approaching a limit — rather than an outage already in progress; the alarm’s own severity and description say which
actions: Open the Alarms view to see the alarm's time, severity, type, description, and region.
Match the alarm type to the relevant section of this guide (for example, a funds alarm relates to Billing, Account State & Licensing; a CPS alarm relates to Capacity & Limits).
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the alarm's described condition doesn't match what you're observing, or if a Critical/Major alarm doesn't clear after the underlying condition is resolved.
evidence: Alarm time, severity, type, and description
related: Concurrent Call Limit Reached, CPS Limit Reached, Insufficient Funds / Trial Restriction

title: Intermittent Issue With No Currently Active Alarm
status: Intermittent Issue With No Currently Active Alarm
meaning: You experienced a problem, but no alarm is currently active. The absence of a currently active alarm doesn't prove no problem occurred — check Alarm History rather than only the live Alarms view.
causes: The condition was transient and has since cleared
The issue occurred outside the window you're currently viewing
actions: Open Alarm History and search around the specific time the issue was reported, rather than only checking current/active alarms.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes with the specific time of the reported issue if Alarm History shows nothing relevant.
evidence: Timestamp and time zone of the reported issue

title: Caller Cancelled Before Answer
meaning: The caller ended the call attempt before the destination answered.
causes: The caller hung up, pressed end call, or their calling app cancelled the attempt before the destination picked up
actions: No action needed for normal, occasional occurrences.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes only if this is happening at an unusually high rate relative to total call volume.

title: Destination Busy or Declined
meaning: The destination was legitimately busy or actively declined the call.
causes: The destination device signaled it was already in use, or the person/system actively rejected the incoming call
actions: Investigate only if all calls to a destination return busy/declined unexpectedly, multiple destinations are affected, or the result conflicts with the destination's known state.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if busy/decline results conflict with a destination confirmed to be available.

title: Call Completed and Ended Normally
meaning: The call connected and both parties disconnected normally when finished.
causes: Either party ended the call after the conversation concluded, using a standard call-teardown signal
actions: No action needed — this is expected, normal behavior.
escalate: No escalation needed.

title: Conversation Completed as Designed
meaning: The AI Agent conversation reached its intended conclusion and ended.
causes: The AI Agent’s flow or logic reached its defined end state — for example, the caller’s request was resolved or handed off as intended
actions: No action needed — this is expected, normal behavior.
escalate: No escalation needed.

title: Maximum Call Duration Reached (Expected)
meaning: The call ended because it reached a configured maximum-duration limit — this is designed behavior, not a failure.
causes: A configured maximum-duration limit — account-level or on the specific voice entity — was reached, and the call ended automatically as designed
actions: Confirm against the configured maximum duration if you want to verify the exact limit in effect.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the call ended before any configured maximum duration was reached.
related: Call Limit / Maximum Call Duration Reached

title: Old Recording or Transcript No Longer Available (Retention)
status: Old Recording or Transcript No Longer Available (Retention)
meaning: The recording or transcript was removed automatically because it exceeded the account's configured retention period.
causes: The recording or transcript’s age passed the account’s configured retention period, and it was removed automatically
actions: Check the configured retention period against the age of the item you're looking for.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the item should still be within the retention window.

title: No-User-Input Handled Normally
meaning: The caller was silent, and the AI Agent handled it using its configured no-user-input behavior (such as repeating a prompt, transferring, or ending the call).
causes: The caller didn’t speak or provide input within the expected window, and the agent’s configured no-input handling — a reprompt, fallback message, or graceful call end — took over as designed
actions: Review the prompt/Flow configuration if you want to confirm the exact configured behavior.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the observed handling doesn't match what's configured.

title: User Signed Out
meaning: The user signed out of Live Hub, either manually or because their session ended.
causes: The user clicked sign out, or their session ended due to an inactivity timeout or an administrator-forced sign-out
actions: Sign in again to continue.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if sign-outs are happening much more frequently than expected during active use.

title: Teams Connection Shows 'Creating'
meaning: A newly created Teams connection can briefly show a Creating status before becoming Active. This is expected provisioning behavior.
causes: The connection was created recently and Microsoft Teams hasn’t finished provisioning it yet — this is a normal, temporary state
actions: Allow a reasonable amount of time for provisioning before treating this as a problem.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the connection remains in Creating status well beyond the expected provisioning time.
evidence: How long it has shown Creating

title: Alternate Routing / Multiple Call Records for One Attempt
status: Alternate Routing / Multiple Call Records for One Attempt
meaning: You see more than one call record for what felt like a single call attempt. This can happen when a routing group fails over to an alternate destination, or a transfer occurred.
causes: A routing group’s failover logic tried more than one destination for the same call attempt, and each attempt was logged as its own call record
actions: Search for related call records sharing the same SID to see the full sequence.
escalate: Contact AudioCodes if the sequence of records doesn't match the configured routing group priorities or expected transfer behavior.
